title: Nike Is Restructuring the Business | NKE Stock Deep Dive Part 3
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Part 3 of Parkevtate's Nike deep dive — published October 12 but only released from members-only access on October 14 — examines Nike's 'Pace' restructuring as sales decline, consumers trade down or switch brands, and tariff exposure rises on its overseas manufacturing base, with the stock near its 52-week low. The supply chain is being made more flexible, including a new Bengaluru, India campus that reduces reliance on Southeast Asia and China, where tariffs are steeper and relations more fraught; he notes US production still does not pencil out on cost or bureaucracy. Significant job cuts are expected. On the numbers: Q4 revenue of $11.2B was down 4% year over year, and while gross margin improved slightly as some tariffs lapsed, mix shifted toward lower-margin wholesale. His longest-running disappointment — repeated for roughly two years — is discounting: Nike keeps promising more full-price selling yet must keep promoting to clear stale inventory, which he argues requires cutting production so fresher product can hold price. No buy/hold/sell verdict is given in this part (it lands in members-only Part 5), so the call recorded is NKE UNCERTAIN; his prior explicit stance was HOLD on October 2, with no flip. One gross-margin figure is garbled in the auto-captions.
